strengths: Clear and well-motivated problem formulation that identifies specific limitations of existing methods (OPTQ and GPFQ) and proposes a principled unification

Rigorous theoretical contributions with formal proofs establishing equivalence between interpretable formulation and efficient implementation; novel interpretation of OPTQ showing it implicitly corrects cumulative quantization error
Exceptional practical efficiency: achieves 13.8× algorithm speedup and 3.6× pipeline speedup despite correcting more error sources; memory reduction from O(mN) to O(N²) (18× for Llama3.1-8B)
First work to systematically isolate rounding algorithm impact by controlling quantization grids across transformation methods, demonstrating consistency across multiple scenarios

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple bit widths (2-bit to 4-bit), quantization types (weight-only, weight-activation, KV cache), and transformation methods with consistently strong improvements (45.3× perplexity improvement at 1.58-bit)
Significant practical impact: quantization in 45 minutes vs 1300 GPU hours for alternatives; drop-in replacement with no inference overhead; directly applicable to deployed systems
Strong reproducibility: uses public models/datasets, clear experimental setup with documented hyperparameters, code to be open-sourced
weaknesses: Evaluation limited to Llama3 model family only; generalizability claims to other architectures (Mistral, Phi, Gemma, etc.) unvalidated; no empirical end-to-end inference efficiency measurements on deployed hardware
Notable computational overhead: 2× quantization time compared to OPTQ limits practical adoption; requires two forward passes vs OPTQ's one, tradeoff not thoroughly analyzed

Critical experimental design choices lack proper justification: block-level error correction standard practice but impact not ablated, weight ordering by H diagonal not compared to alternatives, regularization parameter λ differs between settings without sensitivity analysis

Incremental theoretical novelty: core contribution combines existing ideas (error correction from GPFQ + weight diffusion from OPTQ); Cholesky decomposition is standard; gap between theoretical full-layer and practical block-level formulation not deeply investigated

Missing ablation studies on: contribution of each error source (weights, activations, previous layers), block-wise vs full-layer correction approaches, hyperparameter sensitivity, which factors drive performance gains

Dense mathematical presentation requiring multiple theorems to connect abstract formulation to Algorithm 1; notation-heavy and less accessible despite rigor; cryptic title with unclear Chronos connection

Narrow evaluation scope using only WikiText2 perplexity and zero-shot reasoning tasks; no analysis of performance on diverse downstream tasks or failure cases; no investigation of min-max grid limitation or non-uniform quantization compatibility

strengths: Identifies and formalizes a genuine gap in PTQ literature: explicitly handling mismatched inputs (X vs X̃) from previous quantization errors, which OPTQ overlooks

Strong theoretical contributions: Theorems 3.1-3.2 prove elegant equivalent formulations enabling 13.8× speedup and 18× memory reduction; Corollary 3.4 provides novel geometric insight into OPTQ as cumulative error correction via orthogonal projections
Superior experimental methodology: fixes quantization grids to isolate rounding algorithm impact, enabling fair comparison across methods and transformations—this approach is methodologically novel

Comprehensive and consistent empirical validation: systematic evaluation across 2/1.58/3/4-bit quantization, weight-only and weight-activation settings, multiple models (Llama3, Qwen3), and numerous transformation methods (HIP, MagR, SmoothQuant, etc.). Improvements largest in challenging settings (2-bit: 1.4-4.9× vs OPTQ)
Excellent reproducibility and practical impact: integrated into open-source Brevitas library with public code, detailed hyperparameters, pseudocode, and honest scope discussion
Efficient implementation: significant memory (18×) and computational (13.8× microbenchmark) improvements with calibration overhead decreasing from 19.7% to 8.7% as model size increases
weaknesses: Incremental core novelty: the conceptual idea of alternating error correction and diffusion is straightforward; main contribution is engineering (handling mismatched inputs and efficient implementation) rather than algorithmic innovation. Theorem 3.2 acknowledged as 'not novel' by authors

Lack of statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, error bars, or significance testing. Main results appear single-run; only microbenchmark averaged over 3 seeds. Modest improvements in many settings (Table 3 W4: 0.1-0.5 accuracy points, 0.1-0.3 perplexity points) lack significance quantification

Limited experimental scope: evaluation restricted to LLMs (Llama3, Qwen3); generalization to vision/other domains unknown. Only scaled min-max grids explored; authors suggest non-uniform quantization could improve results but don't explore this

Theoretical gaps: no convergence analysis, approximation guarantees relative to NP-hard problem, or error bounds. Limited intuition for why method works empirically beyond triangle inequality argument (Section D)

Fairness of comparisons: GPTAQ exhibits NaN instability (footnote 3) suggesting implementation issues not investigated; different dampening strategies (α=1e-6 vs 1e-3) suggest unequal tuning effort; block-wise resetting (X̃=X per block) appears ad-hoc and lacks ablation justifying this choice

Underexplored design decisions: why different α for weight-only vs weight-activation? Why combine HIP+MagR? What is first iteration optimization (Theorem E.2) contribution? Missing ablations and sensitivity analyses

Practical trade-offs underexplored: two-pass requirement increases calibration time 9-19% (Table 5). Trade-off between quality gain and computational cost lacks thorough analysis across deployment scenarios
Limited novelty scope: concurrent work on quantization geometry (Birnick 2025, Chen et al. 2025) mentioned but not compared; recent continuous optimization methods not thoroughly evaluated against

strengths: Rigorous mathematical framework with technically sound theorems and complete proofs; particularly Theorems 3.1-3.2 on efficient reformulation and Corollary 3.4 on OPTQ interpretation
Significant algorithmic efficiency improvements (18× memory reduction, 13.8× algorithmic speedup) with practical engineering benefits
Identifies and formalizes important practical problem of error accumulation from quantized layers (Equation 2 vs Equation 1), not previously explicitly addressed
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across model families, bit-widths, quantization scenarios, and transformation methods with detailed ablations and hyperparameter sensitivity analysis
Addresses realistic setting combining weight-only, weight-activation, and KV cache quantization scenarios with reproducible code integrated into Brevitas library
weaknesses: Limited core algorithmic novelty—alternating error correction and diffusion is straightforward; main contribution is efficient implementation via Theorems 3.1-3.2, but the result that qt=Q(w_t^(t-1)) for t≥2 is somewhat expected once formulation established

Incremental practical improvements in standard settings—2-bit 8B Llama3: 10.4→9.3 perplexity (~10%), 0-shot accuracy nearly identical (55.2→55.8); larger gains only at unusual bit widths (1.58-bit) or aggressive scenarios (W4A4KV4) with limited practical deployment

Deliberately restricted to scaled min-max quantization grid; authors acknowledge results could improve with non-uniform grids or vector quantization; grid optimization via linear search could neutralize algorithmic improvements, limiting generality

Baseline comparison fairness concerns: different dampening schemes (OPTQ λ=1% diagonal vs Qronos λ=α·σ₁) without justification; GPTAQ shows unexplained instability (NaN values); missing comparisons with recent continuous optimization methods

Incomplete theoretical analysis—no convergence guarantees, no characterization of when (X-Ẋ)W correction is significant vs negligible; Figure 3 shows error accumulation for only one setting; triangle inequality bound in Section D is loose

strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation identifying the mismatch between inputs X and X̃ (original vs quantized), addressing a real limitation of OPTQ

Solid theoretical contributions: Theorem 3.1 showing RTN equivalence for t≥2, Theorem 3.2 enabling efficient Cholesky-based implementation, and Corollary 3.4 providing novel geometric interpretation of OPTQ's cumulative error correction
Practical implementation optimizations achieving 18× memory reduction (O(mN) to O(N²)) through clever reformulation with G and H matrices, directly addressing real deployment constraints

Rigorous and comprehensive experimental methodology: multiple quantization settings (2-bit to 4-bit, weight-only, weight-activation, KV cache), multiple model families (Llama3, Qwen3), and multiple transforms (HIP, MagR, SmoothQuant, etc.), with careful isolation of rounding algorithm impact by fixing quantization grids
Consistent empirical improvements across all evaluated settings, with insightful observation that larger gains appear at more challenging quantization tasks (W4A4KV4 > W4A4 > W4)
Clear presentation with well-designed figures and comprehensive appendix with full proofs
weaknesses: Limited core algorithmic novelty: Sequential greedy rounding is well-established (OBQ, OPTQ, GPFQ). The main contribution of handling (X, X̃) mismatch is incremental. Theorems 3.1-3.2 primarily establish equivalences rather than revealing new algorithmic insights.

Modest practical improvements at realistic bit-widths: 4-bit weight-only quantization shows ~0.1-0.3 perplexity differences (Table 3), which are statistically marginal. Strongest improvements occur at extreme quantization (1.58-bit) rarely used in practice.

Evaluation scope limitations: (1) restricted to min-max quantization grids despite acknowledging potential benefits of more sophisticated grids; (2) single domain (LLMs only); (3) no exploration of generalization to computer vision or other NLP tasks

Baseline comparison issues: GPTAQ exhibits NaN entries in Table 4 attributed to 'instability,' undermining direct comparison. Insufficient investigation into whether this reflects unfair comparison or fundamental issues.

Incomplete mechanistic analysis: Paper observes that improvements increase with quantization difficulty but doesn't explain why. Limited exploration of when/why handling (X, X̃) mismatch helps more for activation quantization than weight-only (beyond observation in Section 4.2).

Hyperparameter and design choice justification: Different α damping values for weight-only (1e-6) vs weight-activation (1e-3) appear ad-hoc with no ablation studies. Dampening strategy differs from OPTQ without clear justification. Calibration sensitivity analysis missing.

Overstated practical overhead claims: Microbenchmark speedup of 13.8× doesn't translate to practice; Table 5 shows 8.7%-19.7% actual calibration overhead. Memory reduction (18×) applies only to first iteration, with subsequent iterations already using efficient Cholesky.

Missing ablation studies and sensitivity analyses: No ablation on damping strategy, calibration data size sensitivity, or comparison of quantization grid designs. Limited investigation into failure modes (e.g., GPTAQ instability).
